text:
jamal: Heads up — started seeing intermittent hangs/timeouts on 8-node TP jobs during ramp tests this morning. ~30% repro when we push batch size up and enable dynamic batching. Logs show rendezvous timeouts and one instance of rank desync. Posting what I've got so far.

mira: Ugh, saw one of those in prod-ish yesterday too. Any obvious correlation with KV cache churn or kernel selection changes?

jamal: Initial correlation: spikes happen when sequence-length variance increases (some requests 2x longer). Profiler shows all-reduce tail latency spikes at same timestamps. Kernel selector also switches to the slower path for long sequences which seems to misalign buffers.

alex: Can you paste the rendezvous log snippet?

jamal: Sure — snippet below from the runtime logs right when the job stalled:

```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] rank=2 WARN rendezvous: waiting for peers, elapsed=118s
[2026-03-15T09:14:14Z] rank=2 ERROR rendezvous: timeout waiting for rank=3 (last heard=115s ago)
[2026-03-15T09:14:16Z] runtime: rank 3 lost connection, entering drain
[2026-03-15T09:14:20Z] tp: detected kv_cache_version mismatch: local=42 remote=41
[2026-03-15T09:14:22Z] runtime: aborting step -> partial allreduce observed
```

mira: That kv_cache_version line is suspicious. We don't expect kv cache to change mid-run unless the kernel selection/quantization path mutated the cache layout.

toni: Is there a config that triggers a lazy kv cache rebuild across ranks? I remember a recent change to avoid eager eviction.

jamal: We have a lazy rebuild in place: when kernel selector chooses a different code path it sets kv_layout_hint and we recompute offsets lazily. Hypothesis: when different ranks choose different kernels (due to local sequence distribution) the kv layout hints diverge and our rendezvous assumes identical cache layouts. That mismatch can cause one rank to write different KV sizes, confusing the all-reduce buffer bounds -> timeout.

alex: Interesting. Any repro script?

jamal: Minimal repro attached (ran on 8xA100): we run mixed sequence-length traffic with rng skew and force kernel_probe to choose by-length. Command I used:

```
./run_tp_job --nodes=8 --microbatch=2 --seq-dist=skewed --kernel-probe=per-rank --kv-lazy=true --log-level=debug
```

mira: Ran that locally on staging with an instrumentation build. Observations:
- With kv-lazy=true and kernel-probe=per-rank: 6/20 runs hit rendezvous timeout.
- Forcing kernel-probe=global (same kernel chosen across ranks) => 0/20 timeouts.
- Forcing kv-lazy=false (eager rebuild at kernel change) => 1/20 timeouts (still flaky).

toni: Nice triage. So divergence is the likely root. Could also interact with all-reduce chunking: if one rank reports a different tensor size the all-reduce protocol goes out of sync.

jamal: I profiled all-reduce tail times with our tracer. Relevant excerpt (p99 shows spikes):

```
allreduce_latency_ms p50=2.8 p90=12.4 p99=312.7
seqlen_variance=0.67
kernel_path_switches=avg 0.9/s per-rank
kv_layout_switches=avg 0.4/s per-rank
```

alex: p99=312ms is huge for an allreduce. That explains stalled steps. Does the kernel switch happen mid-step or only between steps?

jamal: It can happen mid-step because we probe at op start to pick optimized kernels given the effective sequence length. If different microbatches get routed differently per-rank we can end up with topology mismatch mid-step.

toni: We should add a safety: annotate rendezvous with kv_cache_version and fail fast with a clear error before entering partial all-reduce. Right now it logs the mismatch then keeps trying, causing long waits.

mira: Agreed. Quick mitigation: make kernel selection deterministic across ranks for the step. Options: (A) global probe at step start, broadcast choice; (B) derive kernel choice from agreed-upon max_seqlen in step; (C) force eager kv rebuild whenever a kernel choice would diverge.

jamal: I prototyped (A) yesterday. Results: broadcasting kernel_id at step start eliminated the timeouts in 30 runs. Downsides: small extra latency on step start (~2ms) and some suboptimal kernel choices for ranks with smaller seqs. Throughput impact measured: -3% throughput, but stable.

alex: That's an acceptable trade for now. We can ship as a safety guard in the next patch release and iterate on smarter heuristics.

toni: Also add an assert in the all-reduce handshake: compare declared tensor sizes and kv_cache_version before any heavy comm. If mismatch -> abort step with structured error (no 2-minute rendezvous wait).

jamal: I'll open a PR with three commits: 1) deterministic kernel choice broadcast, 2) handshake check for kv_cache_version + buffer bounds, 3) diagnostic metric exposing per-step kernel_id distribution.

ci-bot: jamal pushed branch jamal/tp-kernel-broadcast -> CI queued.

mira: Quick experiment notes (after applying jamal's branch locally): 50/50 seq-skew test, 100 runs: 0 timeouts, p99 allreduce latency reduced from 312.7ms to 48.9ms (huge improvement).

alex: Nice. Can we also log kernel_id per-rank with the trace to help postmortems? Toni's diagnostic will help.

toni: I'll add a small dashboard: kernel_id heatmap per deployment + kv_cache_version churn over time. That should make regressions visible.

sre-oncall: From an operational POV we should add an alert: if rendezvous time > 30s for >3 steps in a job, mark the job degraded and surface to oncall rather than let it stall.

jamal: Good call. Adding degraded alert and a Runbook entry: "When rendezvous timeout with kv_cache_version mismatch: enable kernel-broadcast, run repro script, collect trace logs (trace.tar.gz) and kv layout dumps from each rank."

mira: One more data point: disabling lazy kv entirely regresses throughput on normal workloads by ~8% (more mem copies). So long-term fix should allow lazy behavior but with deterministic layout negotiation.

jamal: Agreed. Roadmap: short-term safety (broadcast + handshake + alert), mid-term: negotiate kv_layout hint in rendezvous proactively (layout negotiation protocol), long-term: make kernel selector cost-aware across ranks (global optimizer).

alex: When will the PR land?

ci-bot: jamal/tp-kernel-broadcast passed unit tests, integration tests queued.

jamal: I'll follow up with PR link in ~30m. Thanks all for quick triage.

toni: :thumbsup: please add the repro command to the PR description so QE can run it.

mira: Also add the perf snippet to the PR so reviewers know expected impact numbers.

jamal: Will do. End of thread — moving to review and patch.
